sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Mandate**: FSI publishes ISFR biennially since 1987. It uses **IRS Resourcesat-2** satellite data.
• **Forest Cover vs. Recorded Forest Area**: **Forest Cover** is based on canopy density (remote sensing), while **Recorded Forest Area** is based on government records (legal status).
• **Canopy Density Classes**: Very Dense Forest (VDF >70%), Moderately Dense Forest (MDF 40-70%), Open Forest (OF 10-40%), and Scrub (<10%).
• **Key Metric**: The report calculates 'Carbon Stock' in India's forests, which is a critical indicator for India's **NDC (Nationally Determined Contributions)** under the Paris Agreement.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Green India Mission**: Uses ISFR data to monitor afforestation targets.
• **CAMPA Funds**: Allocation of funds based on forest loss/gain data provided by FSI.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Difficulty in distinguishing between natural forests and commercial plantations in satellite data.
• **Solutions**: Integration of LiDAR technology for better vertical structure assessment.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'V-M-O-S' (Very, Moderately, Open, Scrub).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Order of canopy density from highest (VDF >70%) to lowest (Scrub <10%).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often equates 'Recorded Forest Area' with 'Forest Cover'. Remember: RFA is legal/administrative; Forest Cover is physical/canopy-based.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ecological Integrity' when discussing the quality of forest cover, not just the quantity.

keyTakeaways: ISFR is a biennial report, not annual.
Forest Cover includes all lands >1 hectare with >10% canopy density.
Tree Cover is measured via ground inventory, not satellite mapping.
